status_meanings.internal: Internally derived/reconstructed candidate or scoped diagnostic

Contractive finite-precision sparse nc acquisition; full proof and exact costs:
 work/cycle1/algebra_contracting_sparse_theorem.txt
For unknown f=sum_(j<=s) c_j w_j over Q, SUPPLIED n,s, maximum word length D,
and numerator/denominator bit-height H, one FULL approximate matrix query at
dimension 2s recovers every ordered word and rational coefficient exactly.
Explicit upper-triangular dyadic tuple, B a power of two >n+1:
 T_i(a,b)=binom(b,a) i^(b-a)/B^b, 0<=a<=b<2s.
Every T_i has induced column-sum norm 1, query-entry bits O(s log(n+1)).
Required certified absolute precision per entry:
 P=O(H+sD log(n+1)+s+log(s+1)).
The deterministic decoder is polynomial BIT time in n,s,D,H. This includes
actual output word lengths; there is no poly(log D) output claim.

Mechanism/proof in six steps:
1. v(z)T_i=v((z+i)/B). Word code
 alpha(w)=B^-l*(1+sum_t i_t B^(t-1))
is injective, in (0,1] and separated by >=B^-D. Column sums of the response
are moments t_k=sum_j c_j alpha_j^k, k=0,...,2s-1.
2. Set U=2^(s-1) B^(D(s-1)), K=2^H s^2 U^2. Lagrange interpolation bounds
Vandermonde inverse norm by sU. The signed Hankel matrix has actual rank r and
ALL nonzero eigenvalues have absolute value >=1/K. This remains true for signed
cancellation, since its restriction is R diag(c_j) R^T and |c_j|>=2^-H.
3. With sufficiently precise noisy moments, exact rational inertia of
 M_tilde +/- I/(4K)
recovers r. Use rational symmetric Schur elimination, including 2-by-2 pivots;
no floating SVD or exact zero test of a noisy matrix is substituted.
4. Solve the approximate leading-r Hankel recurrence. The true annihilator of
 beta_j=B^D alpha_j
is monic with integer coefficients. Proved inverse perturbation bounds make
the scaled approximate coefficients accurate to <1/8; integer rounding recovers
the annihilator exactly.
5. Exact Sturm isolation recovers the promised integer roots with polynomial
degree/height and O(D log B) interval depths. Base-B digits recover each word.
6. Solve the exact-node Vandermonde system with noisy moments. Its coefficient
errors are <1/(8*2^(2H)); continued fractions recover rational coefficients with
denominators <=2^H. Exact rational full-response recovery is unnecessary.

Precision is not free acquisition: dense query input costs O(ns^3 log(n+1)) bits
under an ordinary explicit matrix interface, response transfer costs
O(s^2(P+H+log(s+1))) bits, plus the target oracle's evaluation/precision cost.
The active matrix service and the supplied D,H are substantive. This is not an
arbitrary fixed-noise, passive, finite-field, or general-rational-circuit learner.
Same-field dimension 2s is optimal across unrestricted coefficients/degrees for
one fixed tuple, by splitting a minimal polynomial. No optimality claimed for
competitors whose tuple may depend on bounded D,H.

Important falsification: each T_i embeds in a (2s+1)-state column-stochastic
matrix [[T_i,0],[ones-ones*T_i,1]]. For positive coefficients summing to 1, the
response is a physical mixture-of-word Markov channel. But THIS fixed tuple can
need exponential sampling: with n=2,s=1,B=4, distinguish words 1^D and
2 1^(D-1). Their informative output probabilities differ by delta=4^-D,
per-trial KL<5 delta^2, so 2/3-success binary discrimination requires at least
(2/45)*16^D independent channel uses. This is a specific-query obstruction,
not a lower bound against every active stochastic design.

CONTRACTIVE ONE-QUERY SPARSE NC ACQUISITION WITH CERTIFIED FINITE PRECISION
7 October 2026. Internal proof and finite diagnostics; historical priority UNKNOWN.
This is a bounded-degree/height extension of N68, using the affine mechanism in
Lakhani--Mukhopadhyay, ECCC TR26-120. Prony, inertia, and rational recovery are old.

THE EXACT INTERFACE
Supply integers n,s>=1, D>=0, H>=0. Unknown
 f=sum_(j=1)^r c_j w_j in Q<x_1,...,x_n>, r<=s,
has distinct ordered words of length <=D and nonzero reduced rational coefficients
c_j=a_j/b_j with |a_j|<=2^H and 1<=b_j<=2^H. A zero polynomial is allowed.
An active oracle accepts exact rational n-tuples of m-by-m matrices and returns
the FULL matrix response approximated by rational dyadics, with a CERTIFIED
entrywise absolute-error bound chosen by the caller. The oracle's evaluation,
precision production, input transfer, and output transfer are charged.

Construction: m=2s; choose power of two B>n+1. For 0<=a<=b<m, put
 T_i(a,b)=binom(b,a)*i^(b-a)/B^b; put T_i(a,b)=0 for a>b.
Every T_i is nonnegative, has induced column-sum norm exactly 1, and has
O(s log(n+1))-bit entries. The tuple is independent of D,H.

THEOREM
One approximate FULL response at this tuple suffices for deterministic EXACT
reconstruction, using poly(n,s,D,H) bit computation and
 P=O(H+s D log(n+1)+s+log(s+1))
certified fractional precision bits per response entry. Returned integer parts
need at most H+log(s+1)+O(1) bits. No fixed-precision, degree-free, passive-sample,
or succinct-circuit-size capability is asserted. The bit cost of creating the
oracle response is not included for free in the decoder bound.

EXPLICIT SAFE PRECISION
Define
 U=2^(s-1)*B^(D(s-1)), K=2^H*s^2*U^2, m=2s,
 C_ann=32*K*s*m*2^s*B^(Ds), C_coef=8*s*U*m*2^(2H),
 epsilon_0=1/max(C_ann,C_coef).
An entrywise error epsilon<epsilon_0 suffices. For example, ask for at least
 ceil(log2(max(C_ann,C_coef)))+4
fractional bits, with a certified dyadic approximation error <=1.5*2^(-P).
The precise constants are conservative. P is linear in H, rather than sH.

PROOF: AFFINE WORD CODES AND CONTRACTION
For v_m(z)=(1,z,...,z^(m-1)), the binomial theorem gives
 v_m(z)T_i=v_m((z+i)/B).
Consequently, for w=i_1...i_l,
 alpha(w)=B^(-l)*(1+sum_(t=1)^l i_t B^(t-1)), alpha(empty)=1,
 v_m(1)T_w=v_m(alpha(w)).
Nonempty codes are in (0,1). Their numerator has lowest base-B digit i_1+1 in
{2,...,n+1}, strictly less than B; thus it is not divisible by B. The least
integer l with B^l alpha integral is exactly the word length. This proves
injectivity. The lowest digit minus 1 is i_1; successive digits give i_2,...,i_l.
In particular, distinct codes for words of length <=D are separated by >=B^-D.

Column b of T_i has sum ((i+1)/B)^b<=1; column 0 has sum 1. Hence ||T_i||_1=1.
For F=f(T), ||F||_1<=sum_j |c_j|<=s 2^H. Approximate response Y with entrywise
error <=epsilon gives moments t_tilde_k=sum_a Y(a,k) with
 |t_tilde_k-t_k|<=m epsilon,
 t_k=sum_j c_j alpha_j^k, 0<=k<m.

PROOF: EXACT RANK FROM APPROXIMATE MOMENTS
Let V_r=(alpha_j^k)_(0<=k<r,1<=j<=r). Row j of V_r^-1 is the coefficient vector
of the Lagrange polynomial
 prod_(i!=j)(z-alpha_i)/(prod_(i!=j)(alpha_j-alpha_i)).
Since 0<alpha_i<=1 and differences are >=B^-D, every inverse entry is at most
 2^(r-1) B^(D(r-1)) <= U
in absolute value. Thus ||V_r^-1||_2<=r U<=s U.

The s-by-s true Hankel matrix M=(t_(a+b)) has rank r and factors

artifacts.reported_claim_excerpt:
Bounded single-site biases and reversibility do not imply affordable acquisition,
even when the learner knows a two-model hypothesis class and receives every
update attempt and its exact time. An explicit empty-graph/complete-graph pair
requires exponentially long observation from an allowed initial state. This
prevents a broad transfer from exact acquisition, bounded local rates, or the
recent dynamical learning results to a general passive acquisition theorem.

There is also a positive, genuinely acquired representation: observed flip-count
covariances recover unknown disjoint parity hyperedges in polynomial observation
time and computation, without observing failed attempts or waiting for the full
configuration chain to mix. The count law has a two-state quotient which is
proved below; the unknown groups are learned rather than supplied. This is a
restricted family and ordinary covariance analysis is the competent method.

1. EXPONENTIAL OBSERVATION LOWER BOUND, WITH A TWO-HYPOTHESIS COMPARATOR

Interface. Let n>=2 be even, theta>0 fixed, and X(0)=(+1,...,+1). The unknown
potential is one of the two explicitly supplied descriptions
  psi_0(x)=theta sum_i x_i,
  psi_1(x)=theta |sum_i x_i|.
Each site has an independent unit-rate clock and at its rings is heat-bath
resampled for pi_b(x) proportional to exp(psi_b(x)). There are no interventions
or resets. The learner may observe the entire configuration path, all clocks,
all failed attempts, and exact times up to a fixed horizon T, and use arbitrary
computation, retention and randomness. It must recover the dependency graph
with error <=delta<1/2 under each hypothesis.

The graph for psi_0 is empty. The graph for psi_1 is complete: its conditional
field at i is theta sign(sum_{j!=i}x_j), and that odd sum can be changed from -1
to +1 by any other site with the remaining n-2 spins balanced. Under BOTH
models every actual conditional field has magnitude theta, so every resampling
probability lies in [1/(1+exp(2theta)), exp(2theta)/(1+exp(2theta))]. This is not
a zero-rate/frozen-state construction.

THEOREM. If both errors are <=delta, necessarily
  T >= (1-2delta) cosh(theta)^n / [n exp(2theta)].

Proof. Couple the clocks and update uniforms. At every configuration with
magnetization M=sum_i x_i>0, all flips lead to M-2x_i>=0; hence the two
potential increments and update laws are identical. The paths couple until
H=inf{t:M(t)=0}. Under psi_0, spins are independent at deterministic time t,
with mean m_t=tanh(theta)+(1-tanh(theta))exp(-t). Consequently
  E_0 exp(-theta M_t)
    =[cosh(theta)-m_t sinh(theta)]^n <= cosh(theta)^(-n),
  Pr_0(M_t<=2) <= exp(2theta) cosh(theta)^(-n).
Entry to M=0 comes from M=2 and has total instantaneous rate at most n.
The compensator/union bound therefore gives
  Pr_0(H<=T) <= n T exp(2theta) cosh(theta)^(-n).
This bounds total variation between the FULL observed path laws by coupling.
Any test with both errors <=delta requires TV>=1-2delta, proving the claim.

Costs and limitations. One time unit contains n attempted updates in expectation;
thus the lower bound is also exponential in total expected updates for a fixed
horizon. Processing or caching the full trace cannot create the missing event.
The equally informed likelihood-ratio comparator knows both concise potentials;
its information also first differs at the rare boundary. No computational
hardness assum

artifacts.reported_claim_excerpt:
EXACT CONSTANT-SHEAR MIXED-BOUNDARY TOMOGRAPHY AND COST OBSTRUCTIONS
Companion to materials_inverse.txt. Internally derived proof, not external
validation or a claim of priority. All lengths/stresses nondimensionalized.

A. INTERFACE
Let B={x in R^3:|x|<1}, S=boundary B, n=x on S. Let mu>0 be constant,
lambda in C-infinity(cl B), and 3lambda+2mu>0. Define
  a=1/(lambda+2mu), so 0<a<3/(4mu).
The elastic equation is
  div[lambda(div u)I+2mu e(u)]=0,
  e(u)=(Du+Du^T)/2.
The input is two tangential displacement components and a scalar normal Robin
condition t_n+4mu u_n=g over all of S. The measured output is u_n over S,
or its specified weighted integrals. Dense spatial controls and sensing are
part of the interface. The unknown does not supply interior displacements,
transport frames, a complete DN matrix, or a FEM solver.

The spring coefficient 4mu is calibrated from a separate experiment if mu is
unknown. The model promise that mu is constant must be independently justified.

B. THE PHYSICAL CONSTRUCTION
Take any harmonic polynomial w. Choose known polynomial v with
  div v=0,    mu Delta v=-grad w.
For each homogeneous harmonic component w_ell, ell>=1, set
  v_ell=ell*x_vector*w_ell/[mu(2ell+3)(ell+1)]
        -(ell+3)*r^2*grad w_ell/[2mu(2ell+3)(ell+1)].
Set v_0=0 and sum. Euler's identity gives
  div(x_vector w_ell)=(ell+3)w_ell,
  div(r^2 grad w_ell)=2ell w_ell,
  Delta(x_vector w_ell)=2grad w_ell,
  Delta(r^2 grad w_ell)=(4ell+2)grad w_ell.
Substitution proves the two required properties. No lambda is used.

Solve the scalar Dirichlet Poisson problem
  Delta phi=a w in B,  phi=0 on S,
and put u=v+grad phi. Let d=div u=a w. Then
  L u = mu Delta u+grad[(lambda+mu)div u]
       = mu Delta v+mu grad(a w)+grad[(1-mu a)w]
       = -grad w+grad w=0.
This is exact for arbitrary smooth a in the stated interval.

Let q=partial_n phi. Since phi=0 on S, grad phi=q n there. For any tangent
vector tau, differentiation of grad phi along the sphere gives
  Hess phi(tau,n)=partial_tau q,
  tr_tangent Hess phi=2q,
  Hess phi(n,n)-Delta phi=-2q.
Consequently
  stress(grad phi)n
  = [w-4mu q]n + 2mu grad_S q.
Therefore
  u_t=v_t,
  t_n+4mu u_n=(2mu e(v)n)_n+w+4mu v_n.
These controls only use w, mu, and geometry. They are the claimed mixed
boundary experiment, and output q=u_n-v_n.

A universal approximately sparse lift cannot repair the old exact universal-
monomial obstruction cheaply. The statement below allows arbitrary frame
weights, arbitrary sparse complex matrices, and no representation, continuity,
positivity, homomorphism, or norm assumption on those matrices.

Let 2 <= d <= N, 1 <= s < d, and V:C^d -> C^N be an isometry. Put

  b(d,N,s) = (d-s)/(d-s+1)
             [binom(N,s) binom(d-1,s-1)]^(-1/(d-s)).

If EVERY U in SU(d) has an N-by-N matrix M_U with <=s nonzero entries
per row and ||M_U V - VU||_op <= epsilon, then

  epsilon^2 >= b(d,N,s).                                      (1)

More strongly the Haar-average best possible squared operator error is >=b.
For Haar random U, the probability that ANY such M achieves error <=epsilon
is at most (1-b)/(1-epsilon^2), for epsilon<1. This last bound can be trivial
at small d; it tends to zero in the polynomial-resource regime below.

For monomial lifts (s=1), even if the lift is not required to be unitary,

  N >= [(d-1)/(d epsilon^2)]^(d-1).                            (2)

For d=2^n and log N,s each polynomial in n, b=1-O(poly(n)/2^n).
The universal error must approach 1, the error of the zero matrix. For a
fixed epsilon<1, s=Omega(2^n/(log N+n)) when s<=d/2. Thus polynomial physical
label bits require exponentially many row entries. A common finite frame
cannot cheaply support approximate universal logical operations merely by
abandoning exact intertwining or the group-homomorphism requirement.

(1) is an internally proved candidate lemma, reconstructed below from elementary

not claim a new mathematical technique or a field-breaking theorem. The new

interface and resource inequality, extending the supplied exact-all-word gate.

That target asks only for a common V and positive sparse C,B with protected
invalid states and alpha H <= V*BV <= beta H; B need not preserve ran V.
It does not ask for sparse lifts of every logical unitary. Short selected words,
term-specific frames, sector coupling, noninvariant B, and general Hamiltonian
encodings remain outside (1). Approximate lifts of individual universal gates
also remain outside unless one charges their accumulated word error and the

FULL DERIVATION

Write the rows of V as r_j in C^(1xd); let a_j=||r_j|| and ignore zero rows.
For every s-element coordinate subset S of {1,...,N}, let L_S be the complex
row span of the rows r_i for i in S. It has dimension <=s. There are at most
K=binom(N,s) such subspaces. Define, for a unit row vector z,

  D(z) = min_S ||z - P_(L_S)z||^2,

where projection notation means row-space orthogonal projection. All row
supports of size <=s are covered, since they can be padded to size s.

For any s-row-sparse M, the jth row of MV belongs to one L_S. Consequently

  ||MV-VU||_F^2 >= sum_j a_j^2 D((r_j/a_j)U).

  ||MV-VU||_op^2 >= q_V(U)
     := d^(-1) sum_j a_j^2 D((r_j/a_j)U).                    (3)

For Haar U, each normalized nonzero row (r_j/a_j)U is a Haar unit vector.
No independence of these rows is needed.

1. EXACT MIXED BOSONIC FAMILY

The proposed ordinary-logconcave local-table extension is valid. In fact the
complementary polynomial satisfies the required logconcavity under the strictly
weaker condition

    beta_j(k) := b_j(k)/k! is logconcave with interval support,
    b_j(k)^2 >= k/(k+1) b_j(k-1)b_j(k+1),  1<=k<q_j.          (C)

This is the maximal independently checkable LOCAL rule which works uniformly
over arbitrary copies of an admitted table and every total particle number.
It is NOT necessary for an individual collection of blocks, even if all total
particle numbers of that collection are considered. Exact fixed-instance
certification is given below.

For a two-mode site b=(1,1,g^2), (C) is g^2<=2, covering the full repulsive range
0<=g<=1 plus weak attraction 1<g<=sqrt(2). For q modes with a pair-count filter
b(k)=a^(k(k-1)/2), (C) is a<=q/(q-1). Thus amplitude g^(k(k-1)/2) is covered
when g^2<=q/(q-1). Both boundaries are sharp in the above universal sense.

The closure proof is a consequence of existing Lorentzian normalization and
polarization, not a new foundational logconcavity theorem. The application to
filtered determinant amplitudes and the exact weak-attraction boundary appear
to be additional corollaries to investigate; priority is not established.

EXACT INTERFACE

Input: explicitly supplied full-column-rank A in Q(i)^(m x r), ordered modes
U=[m], a partition U=disjoint union E_j, q_j=|E_j|, and rational tables
b_j(0),...,b_j(q_j)>=0. Each table is positive exactly on [l_j,u_j]. The total
binary input length L includes A and the tables. Require (C), or the stronger
ordinary logconcavity in the proposed claim. Empty table/support is returned
as Z=0. Matrix acquisition/variational optimization is outside the interface.

Define
  w(S)=1_[|S|=r] product_j b_j(|S intersect E_j|),
  a(S)=det(A_S) sqrt(w(S)),
  Z=sum_[|S|=r] |det(A_S)|^2 w(S).
When Z>0 the target state has amplitudes a(S)/sqrt(Z); its Born law is the
normalized summand. A full-rank A alone does not imply Z>0.

Set d=m-r and
  f_A(x)=det(A* diag(x) A)=sum_[|S|=r] |det(A_S)|^2 x^S,
  g_d(x)=sum_[|T|=d] product_j b_j(q_j-|T intersect E_j|) x^T.
Then [x_all] f_A g_d=Z. f_A is real stable/logconcave: for positive x, its
matrix is positive definite and logdet is concave under the positive affine
matrix map. Arbitrary complex spin/orbital mixing in A is allowed. No separate
up/down Slaters, spin conservation, or reality/sign-free amplitude premise.

COMPLEMENTARY CLOSURE PROOF (INCLUDING ZERO ENDPOINTS)

Let beta_j(k)=b_j(k)/k!, which has the same interval support as b_j. On the
integer box 0<=h_j<=q_j, define
  Omega(h)=1_[sum h_j=d] product_j beta_j(q_j-h_j).
Omega is log-M-concave. If x_i>y_i, some j has x_j<y_j because sums agree.
Exchange one unit from i to j in x and back in y. Each pair of arguments in
the two affected beta tables moves toward balance; logconcavity makes the
product weakly increase. Interval support ensures both exchanged vectors
remain supported. This proves the full weighted symmetric exchange rule.

By Brändén–Huh Corollary 3.16,
  F(y)=(product_j q_j!) sum_h Omega(h) y^h / product_j h_j!
is Lorentzian. Its coefficient at h is
  product_j binom(q_j,h_j) b_j(q_j-h_j).
Polarize y_j into the q_j variables of E_j; Proposition 3.1 divides each
coefficient by product_j binom(q_j,h_j). The result is exactly g_d, so it is
Lorentzian and hence logconcave by Theorem 2.30. Ze

artifacts.reported_claim_excerpt:
Positive binary tensor contractions with complementary edge couplers and polynomially evaluable locally log-concave signatures admit relative counting, arbitrarily rare evidence estimation, and conditional sampling in polynomial time, with no dependence on inverse evidence probability or treewidth. The same oracles give inverse maximum-entropy inference with an explicit interiority cost. This is a clean consequence of Chen–Liu's counting theorem, not a new counting mechanism. Equality-coupled tensor networks need an additional complement/gauge condition; quantum amplitude squaring can destroy the local premise.

1. Imported theorem and load-bearing mechanism.
Primary source: Xiaoyu Chen and Kuikui Liu, An FPRAS for Counting Common Bases of Two Matroids, submitted 5 October 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06724 ; full text https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06724v1 . Local math-preserving extraction: work/cycle1/slater_chen_liu_math.txt.
Thm1.6: nonzero nonnegative multiaffine log-concave coefficient measures mu,nu on N variables, value oracles, a positive coefficient/support seed for each, and supplied bounds R_mu,R_nu on positive coefficient ratios. It approximately counts any coefficient of g_mu g_nu with exponent vector in {0,1,2}^N in ~O(N^11 (N+log(R_mu R_nu))^2 epsilon^-2) arithmetic/oracle operations. Thm5.1 gives a sharper N^10 bound in the complementary homogeneous degree case, on EVERY execution; RemarkA.4 gives polynomial bit complexity when rational inputs and rational value oracles have polynomial encoding length. These are imported preprint claims, not measured runtimes.

The key lemma is NOT merely variance small under the current field. Lemma2.5 assumes a gap gamma uniformly over ALL penalty vectors and external fields, single-factor updates, and bounded total removal rate for a coordinate having exactly one copy. For coordinate-copy probabilities p0,p1,p2, reweight its field and remove its local penalty so q0=q2. Poincare on the zero-copy cut indicator gives gamma q0/2 <= q1, hence p0 p2 <= 4t p1^2/gamma^2. Therefore exact complement failure <= N (||gradient Phi||_infinity + 4 sqrt(t)/gamma). The field reweighting is essential. The gap1 premise comes from the Bochner sum of squares (Prop4.2), the translated base weight's upward curvature0, and the overlap penalty dual's curvature1, then an induced-chain/large-field limit (Lemma5.5). Read depths here: exact statements and these load-bearing derivations read; not every page or every auxiliary implementation lemma verified.

LemmaC.1, which is the convenient black box below: for any multiaffine log-concave weight omega with its value oracle, seed and coefficient range, and any matroid M with independence oracle, count sum_{A in B(M)} omega(A). Its reduction takes nu(T)=1[H\T in B(M)] and uses Thm1.6. This is already explicitly in Chen–Liu; the tensor formulation below is our reconstruction.

2. Exact tensor/evidence reduction.
Interface. Let G be a finite loopless multigraph, with m edges, H its N=2m distinct halfedges, and H_v the halfedges incident at v. A local tensor is f_v:2^{H_v}->Q_{>=0}, supplied by a polynomial-bit evaluation algorithm. Require the NONZERO multiaffine polynomial

to be log-concave on strictly positive variables. Supply one A_v with f_v(A_v)>0 and a bound R_v >= max_positive f_v/min_positive f_v. Write Lambda=sum_v

Both diagonal entries are strictly positive. Complement the column index,
retain the row index, and assign x to the former, y to the latter. Its local
polynomial is

 q(x,y)=d+ux+vy+dxy.

The exact coefficient inequality is

 uv-d^2 = 1+2sr+s^2(r^2-c^2-b^2)
        = 1+2sr+2s^2 b|c| > 0.

For a general polynomial a+ux+vy+dxy with nonnegative coefficients and u,v>0,

therefore passes with extra margin; it even satisfies the bivariate stability
criterion ad<=uv, since here a=d. This stronger fact can be proved without a
stability theorem: for Im(x)>0, a potential root has
y=-(a+ux)/(v+dx), whose imaginary part is
-(uv-ad)Im(x)/|v+dx|^2<=0, hence cannot be in the upper half-plane.

The pair gate, already derived by the other auditor, has homogeneous polynomial

Its Hessian eigenvalues are a+b+c, a-b-c, -a+b-c, -a-b+c. The last three are

artifacts.reported_claim_excerpt:
The two-measure exact-once theorem yields a conditional FPRAS for the full thermal trace of easy-plane XXZ interactions with arbitrary Z fields and nonnegative X fields, on arbitrary graphs. It also gives a FULL relative-error FPRAS for their largest eigenvalue, polynomial in binary coefficient length without requiring bounded numerical coupling scale (Section 4c). The gate/trace reduction below is explicit, rational, and has multiplicative error without inverse partition-function dependence. This extends the named source C.17 EPR application, but novelty is not established. Separately, an exact six-variable cubic disproves even homogeneous multiaffine log-concavity closure under full complement; this blocks a blanket equality-tensor transfer.

1. EXACT HAMILTONIAN INTERFACE
Let G=(V,E) be any finite loopless multigraph, with n qubits. Given binary rational coefficients,

 H = sum_{e=uv} [alpha_e (X_u X_v + Y_u Y_v) + gamma_e Z_u Z_v]
                  + sum_v [b_v X_v + c_v Z_v],

assume alpha_e >= |gamma_e|, b_v >= 0, and c_v arbitrary. Given rational beta>0 and 0<epsilon<=1, estimate

 Z_H(beta) = Tr exp(beta H)

with relative error epsilon and success probability at least 3/4, or amplify to 1-delta. The physical Hamiltonian is -H if using the conventional exp(-beta Hamiltonian) convention. No bipartition, planarity, degree, treewidth, or spectral-gap assumption is imposed.

Define r_v=|b_v|+|c_v|,
 C=3 sum_e alpha_e + sum_v r_v,
 D=2C,
 A_e=3 alpha_e I + alpha_e(XX+YY)+gamma_e ZZ,
 A_v=r_v I+b_v X+c_v Z.

Every A_i is real symmetric, positive semidefinite, and entrywise nonnegative. Indeed the edge eigenvalues are 3alpha+gamma (twice), 5alpha-gamma, alpha-gamma, so 0<=A_e and ||A_e||<=6alpha. The vertex eigenvalues are r +/- sqrt(b^2+c^2), so 0<=A_v and ||A_v||<=2r. Hence sum_i A_i=H+CI and sum_i ||A_i||<=D. C=0 is the trivial H=0 case, Z=2^n.

The algorithm has bit cost polynomial in the binary input length L, n, the NUMERICAL quantity beta D, epsilon^{-1}, and log(delta^{-1}), conditional on the every-execution rational-bit implementation asserted in Chen–Liu Remark A.4. It is not claimed polynomial in log(beta D). No exponentially long dense matrix is built.

An edge gate in computational row/column order 00,01,10,11 is

 [ a 0 0 0 ]
 [ 0 b c 0 ]
 [ 0 c b 0 ]
 [ 0 0 0 a ],

where a=1+s(3alpha+gamma), b=1+s(3alpha-gamma), c=2salpha. Keep the row bits, complement the column bits, and label row ends 1,2 and column ends 4,3. The associated half-edge polynomial is

 q=a(x1 x2+x3 x4)+b(x1 x3+x2 x4)+c(x1 x4+x2 x3).

Its Hessian eigenvalues are a+b+c, a-b-c, -a+b-c, -a-b+c. The triangle inequalities hold:
 a-b-c=2s(gamma-alpha)<=0,

 -a-b+c=-2-4salpha<0.
Thus q has at most one positive Hessian eigenvalue, which is exactly the homogeneous nonnegative quadratic log-concavity criterion. This includes |gamma|=alpha and zero off-diagonal weight c=0.

For a vertex field gate, in row/column order 0,1,

With x the complemented column half-edge and y the row half-edge, the polynomial is

 q=sb(1+xy)+[1+s(r+c)]x+[1+s(r-c)]y.

artifacts.reported_claim_excerpt:
No fatal mathematical gap found. The claimed singular-support transport,
strong-convexity stability and O_(M,lambda)(b^(1/8)) bound are valid. The
bounded-Holevo broadcasting=>EB statement is indeed equivalent to its fixed
two-sided-sandwich restriction, after spelling out the routine common-support
channel compression described below. The broad statement remains OPEN.

There is also a sharper valid transport argument: compatible-smoothing
preservation improves from O(b^(1/8)) to O(b^(1/4)) at fixed M,lambda. This
does not remove the exponential-in-accuracy smoothing constants or prove
EB reconstruction. Exact formulas and derivation are below.

1. MINIMIZER / STRONG CONVEXITY / CHANNEL IMPORT

Fix density sigma, M>=1, lambda>0, and K_sigma={tau>=0, tau<=M sigma,
Tr tau<=1}. This is nonempty compact convex in finite dimension. Every
feasible tau is supported on supp(sigma). On that support Q_sigma(tau)
=||sigma^(-1/4)tau sigma^(-1/4)||_2^2 is a positive definite quadratic
form. The root fidelity f(rho,tau) is concave in tau and continuous,
including zero eigenvalues. Thus J=-f+lambda Q has a unique minimizer G.

For Hermitian X supported on sigma, choose its sign unitary U (extended
arbitrarily on the zero eigenspaces). Schatten Holder and Tr sigma=1 give

 ||sigma^(1/4) U sigma^(1/4)||_2 <= ||sigma^(1/4)||_4^2=1,
 ||X||_1=Tr U X <= sqrt(Q_sigma(X)).

For Y=sigma^(-1/4)tau sigma^(-1/4), tau<=M sigma implies
0<=Y<=M sqrt(sigma). Although squaring is not operator-monotone, the
TRACE inequality is valid: Tr[Y(M sqrt(sigma)-Y)]>=0. Therefore
Q_sigma(tau)<=M Tr[Y sqrt(sigma)]=M Tr tau<=M.

The exact quadratic identity and concavity give
J((1-t)tau+t v) <= (1-t)J(tau)+tJ(v)
                  -lambda t(1-t)Q_sigma(v-tau).
Minimality at tau yields J(v)-J(tau)>=lambda(1-t)Q_sigma(v-tau);
letting t down to0 proves the stated strong-convexity gap. No gradient,
boundary differentiability or invertibility of rho is assumed.

For a CPTP T, fidelity data processing applies to subnormalized tau by
writing tau=s omega and using homogeneity sqrt(s). Sandwiched-Renyi-2
DPI similarly gives Q_(T sigma)(T tau)<=Q_sigma(tau): its normalized
form is exp(D_2(omega||sigma))=Q_sigma(omega), and multiplying by s^2
extends it. Since T tau<=M T sigma, all output inverses are on the
appropriate support. Zero tau is trivial. Generalized inverses do not
introduce any condition-number constants.

2. ORIGINAL TRANSPORT CONSTANTS CHECK

Let d_s=||sigma-nu||_1 and tau=sqrt(sigma) A sqrt(sigma), 0<=A<=M I,
extending A by zero outside supp(sigma). Put tau'=sqrt(nu) A sqrt(nu).
It satisfies tau'<=M nu even when the reference supports differ.

Expanding tau'-tau into two square-root-difference terms, Holder gives
||tau'-tau||_1<=2M||sqrt(nu)-sqrt(sigma)||_2<=2M sqrt(d_s)=delta.
If t'=Tr tau'>1, clipping kappa=tau'/t' removes trace t'-1<=delta;
otherwise kappa=tau'. Hence kappa in K_nu and ||kappa-tau||_1<=2delta.
The original 4M sqrt(d_s) distance bound is correct.

The exact bounded-likelihood identity is
Q_sigma(tau)=Tr[A sqrt(sigma) A sqrt(sigma)],
Q_nu(tau')=Tr[A sqrt(nu) A sqrt(nu)].
It remains valid when A has components outside supp(nu), because the
outer sqrt(nu) factors annihilate them. Expanding their difference gives
two terms, each bounded by M^2||sqrt(nu)-sqrt(sigma)||_2. Thus
|Q_nu(tau')-Q_sigma(tau)|<=2M^2 sqrt(d_s). Downward clipping only lowers Q.

The proposed cloned chiral determinant identity and stability proof are valid.
They prove, for EVERY F in C^(n x n) and EVERY t_i in [0,1], that

  Z(z) = sum_(k=0)^n c_k z^k,
  c_k = sum_(|I|=|J|=k) |det F_(I,J)|^2 product_(i in I intersect J) t_i

has only strictly negative real zeros (or is constant). In particular the

Two further internally proved candidates are useful:
(A) Smooth zeros do not invalidate the inequality. With
    alpha=mu({X != 0})>0,
       ||Def X||_2^2 >= 2 V H^2 / alpha,
       W >= 4 nu V H^2 / alpha.
    If alpha=0, X=0 and H=W=0. No integrability of log|X| is assumed.
(B) For nowhere-zero X on connected M and H>0, exact equality forces a
    locally homogeneous frame: on a finite cover, |X|=r is constant and
    there are orthonormal normal fields U+,U- satisfying
       [X,U+]=-H U+,  [X,U-]=H U-,  [U+,U-]=c X
    for a constant c. Its Lie algebra is Sol for c=0 and sl(2,R) for c!=0.
    This is an exact-equality conclusion, not stability near equality.

INPUTS / EXACT INTERFACE
M is a smooth closed Riemannian 3-manifold, V=Vol_g(M), X is smooth and
divergence-free, phi_t is its autonomous particle flow, mu=dVol_g/V, and
H=h_mu(phi_1), with natural logarithms. S=Def X=(nabla X+(nabla X)^*)/2,
and |S| is the Hilbert-Schmidt tensor norm. Time-one means one specified
unit of physical time; equivalently replace H with h_mu(phi_T)/T.
The physical constitutive model audited is
    nabla_X X - 2 nu div S + grad p = F,   nu>0,
where F is force per unit mass and nu is kinematic viscosity. W=integral
g(F,X)dVol is integrated power per unit density. The power identity applies
to every sustaining F,p in this model; it requires no assumption that F is
divergence-free. Changing pressure changes F by a gradient and cannot
change W. Smooth sustaining F always exists by defining it as the residual;
an actuator, force acquisition, and a specified digital interface are absent.

PROOF AUDIT: THE LOAD-BEARING POINTS
1. Moving normal cocycle is correct. Put r=|X|, e=X/r, P=I-e tensor e.
For v=Dphi_t v0 write v=w+a e, w=Pv. Torsion-freeness gives

Projection of its decomposition yields

Since nabla_X e=nabla_e X-e X(log r), and the left side is orthogonal to e,
    nabla_X e=P nabla_e X.
The a terms cancel exactly; there is no omitted moving-frame term:
    P nabla_X w=P nabla_w X.
Q_t=P_(phi_t x) Dphi_t|_(e(x)^perp) is an invertible cocycle because the

1. PRECISE COEFFICIENT THEOREM

Let E_1,...,E_s be disjoint blocks, q_j=|E_j|>=1, m=sum q_j. Each nonnegative
table b_j(0),...,b_j(q_j) has interval positive support, or is identically zero.
Set beta_j(k)=b_j(k)/k!. Suppose every beta_j is logconcave, equivalently

  (k+1)b_j(k)^2 >= k b_j(k-1)b_j(k+1),   1<=k<q_j.             (1)

Then for EVERY t=0,...,m the homogeneous multiaffine polynomial

  g_t(x)=sum_[|T|=t] product_j b_j(q_j-|T intersect E_j|) x^T

is Lorentzian (zero allowed), hence logconcave on the positive orthant.
The statement has no Slater-matrix or spin-separation assumption.

Short proof and prior-art identity. Collapse all variables of E_j to y_j:

  G_t(y)=sum_[|h|=t] product_j [binom(q_j,h_j)b_j(q_j-h_j)] y^h
        =(product_j q_j!) sum_[|h|=t] product_j beta_j(q_j-h_j) y^h/h!.

The log of the normalized coefficient is a sum of one-dimensional concave
functions on a box intersected with |h|=t. For h_i>k_i choose j with h_j<k_j.
Moving one unit from i to j in h and back in k balances both affected pairs;
concavity increases their summed logs. Interval support preserves both moved
vectors. This is precisely M-concavity. BH Corollary 3.16 gives Lorentzian G_t,
and BH Proposition 3.1 polarization divides its coefficients by the binomial

INTERFACE
F is an n-by-n complex matrix (rational complex for algorithms). For an even retained ambient set R, define
 Z_R(F)=sum_{I subset R, |I|=|R|/2} |det F[I,R\I]|^2,
and Z_empty=1. This is the full-paired-basis partition of the restricted pairs (e_i,row_i F), with ambient rows restricted to R. It equals the squared-Gram sum for these full paired bases. For n even and hole set U, put f(U)=Z_{[n]\U}; f vanishes on odd U.

SIGNED-HOLE STABILITY: FULL DERIVATION
Let H be the 2n-by-2n Hermitian chiral matrix
 H=[[0,2F],[2F*,0]],
with coordinate pairs (u_i,v_i). P(u,v)=det(diag(u,v)-H) is real stable: the imaginary part of the matrix is strictly positive definite when every coordinate has positive imaginary part, so the determinant is nonzero. Its coefficients are real because H is Hermitian.

Apply D=2^(-n) product_i (partial_{u_i}+partial_{v_i}), and then set u_i=v_i=x_i. A nonnegative directional derivative preserves stability: introduce a new upper-half-plane variable t by shifting both coordinates by t, differentiate t, and specialize t=0 by Hurwitz. Identification also preserves stability. The result Q_F(x) is nonzero (leading coefficient one), real stable, and multiaffine in the n remaining x_i.

Expand the derivative as the average of principal characteristic polynomials retaining exactly one of u_i,v_i at each site. A selected principal chiral minor with up indices I and down indices J has determinant zero unless |I|=|J|. If |I|=|J|=k and I,J are disjoint, its determinant is (-1)^k 2^(2k)|det F[I,J]|^2. It is retained with probability 2^(-2k). Hence
 Q_F(x)=sum_{U: n-|U| even} (-1)^((n-|U|)/2) Z_{[n]\U}(F) product_{i in U} x_i.  (A)
The factor 2 in H is essential: using sqrt2 would leave unwanted powers of two. This is the full multivariate version of the already proved scalar principal-characteristic average, not a claim that the pair-label polynomial is real stable.

FOUR-HOLE REPAIR
For four distinct indices a,b,c,d, set all other hole variables to zero and multiply Q_F by its constant global sign. The surviving stable polynomial is
 q=Z0 -sum_{ij subset {a,b,c,d}} Zij x_i x_j +Z4 x_a x_b x_c x_d,
where Z0=f(empty), Zij=f({i,j}), Z4=f({a,b,c,d}), all nonnegative. If a specialization is identically zero, use continuity; the desired inequality is immediate whenever Z0 Z4=0.

Real stability of a multiaffine real polynomial implies Rayleigh difference
 (partial_a q)(partial_b q)-q partial_ab q >=0
at all real values of the remaining variables. This follows directly from the bivariate real-affine stability/Mobius criterion bc-ad>=0, so no coefficient-sign assumption is used.

At x_a=x_b=0 its Rayleigh difference is
 Z0 Zab +Zac Zbc x_c^2 +Zad Zbd x_d^2
 +(Zac Zbd+Zad Zbc-Zab Zcd-Z0 Z4)x_c x_d
 +Zcd Z4 x_c^2 x_d^2.
Write A=Z0 Z4, P=Zab Zcd, Q=Zac Zbd, R=Zad Zbc. Set v=x_c x_d>=0 and minimize the two quadratic terms at fixed v. Their infimum is 2 sqrt(QR) v, with zero-coefficient cases obtained by limits. Nonnegativity of the resulting quadratic for all v>=0 gives
 A+P-Q-R <=2 sqrt(QR)+2 sqrt(AP).
Equivalently
 (sqrt A-sqrt P)^2 <=(sqrt Q+sqrt R)^2,
so
 sqrt(Z0 Z4) <=sqrt(Zab Zcd)+sqrt(Zac Zbd)+sqrt(Zad Zbc).  (B)
By Cauchy-Schwarz,
 Z0 Z4 <=3[Zab Zcd+Zac Zbd+Zad Zbc].                    (C)

PRIMARY IMPORTED THEOREM
Hamada and Iwata, A Shortest Augmenting Path Algorithm for Linear Matroid
Parity, arXiv:2610.03030v1, submitted 2 October 2026:
 https://arxiv.org/html/2610.03030v1
Theorem 1.1 gives deterministic UNWEIGHTED linear matroid parity in
O(m r^2 log r) field operations, or O(m r^2) with fast multiplication, for an
r-by-m representation over a field K under uniform field cost. Sections
2.1/2.2 seek and maintain the actual independent paired column witness J.
Rank-deficient matrices are first reduced to full row rank. There is no
large-field or characteristic restriction; odd characteristic also avoids
characteristic-two ambiguity. No weighted optimization theorem is needed.
This is an imported optimization/witness theorem, not a counting theorem.
Its input/output/field-cost interface was checked in the primary text; its
entire augmenting-path proof was not independently re-proved or implemented.

EXACT REDUCTION AND BIT BOUND
Let A be an r-by-m rational-complex matrix with paired columns, and let
L>=1 be its full rational encoding length. Multiply A by the product D of
all positive real/imaginary component denominators. Then G=DA is Gaussian
integer, D has O(L) bits, and the nonzero common scalar preserves column
independence over Q(i). A loose bound is |G_ij|<=2^(2L+1).

Any nonzero s-by-s minor delta, s<=r, obeys
 |delta|<=s! 2^((2L+1)s).
Its Gaussian norm N(delta)=delta conjugate(delta) is a positive integer.
For r>=1 the computable numeric integer
 B=1+2r ceil(log2(max{2,r}))+(4L+2)r
satisfies 1<=N(delta)<2^B. B itself, not just its bit length, is polynomial
in r,L. The rank-zero case is trivial.

Choose a nonzero square minor delta of an unknown optimal independent
paired set's nu columns. Among B+1 distinct odd primes some p avoids its
norm: otherwise their product, at least 3^(B+1)>2^B, would divide the smaller
positive integer N(delta). The algorithm need not know delta or the optimum.

DETERMINISTIC PRIME / FIELD CONSTRUCTION
Sieve up to x=2(B+2)^4 and take the first B+1 odd primes; x is polynomial
as a numeric value. An elementary proof that the sieve succeeds avoids an
extra prime-distribution import. For even x,
 binom(x,x/2)>=2^x/(x+1).
For every prime p<=x, its valuation in this binomial is a sum of at most
floor(log_p x) zero/one terms, so p to that valuation is at most x. Hence
 pi(x) log x >= x log2-log(x+1).
With M=B+2>=3 and x=2M^4, log x<=M^2, log(x+1)<=2M^2, and log2>=1/2.
Therefore pi(x)>=(M^4-2M^2)/M^2=M^2-2>=M=B+2. Excluding 2 leaves the
required B+1 odd primes. Sieve time/space is polynomial in r,L.

For p congruent 1 mod4, scan the p residues to find rho^2=-1 modp, and map
a+ib to a+b rho in F_p. Numeric p is polynomial in B, so this exhaustive
root construction is polynomial and deterministic. For p congruent 3 mod4,
use the explicit field F_p[t]/(t^2+1) and map i to t. Arithmetic/inversion
has polynomial bit cost in log p; no randomized extension or factor oracle

 Q(x) = sum_U (-1)^((n-|U|)/2) f(U) x^U.              (1)
The audit below verifies its construction and then proves: for any even S,T and any a in D=S symmetric-difference T,
 sqrt(f(S)f(T)) <= sum_{j in D\{a}}
   sqrt(f(S symmetric-difference {a,j})
        f(T symmetric-difference {a,j})).             (2)
There is no assumption that S and T are disjoint or that their complements have no common occupied core. Thus |S|=4, |T|=2, |D|=6, n>=8 is covered directly.

which is nonvanishing whenever all Re(z_i)>0. For (1) this follows from

Indeed i maps the open right half-plane to the open upper half-plane, and the phases of every even-support coefficient in (1) cancel.

If f(S)f(T)=0, (2) is immediate. In the remaining case both endpoints are strictly positive. Make the simultaneous full reciprocal twist on T:

Because h is multiaffine, this is a polynomial with exact coefficient formula

The map z->1/z preserves the open right half-plane, and the prefactor z^T is nonzero there. Hence h_T is right-half-plane stable. As |T| is even, its support is still even.

1. THE GENERAL COEFFICIENT THEOREM
Let V be a finite ground set. Suppose

 h(x)=sum_{U subset V} f(U) x^U

is nonzero, multiaffine, has real coefficients f(U)>=0, vanishes on every odd
U, and has no zero whenever Re(x_i)>0 for every i. Then for any even S,T and
a in D=S symmetric-difference T,

 sqrt(f(S)f(T))
   <= sum_{j in D, j!=a}
        sqrt(f(S symmetric-difference {a,j})
             f(T symmetric-difference {a,j})).                 (E)

Cases with f(S)f(T)=0 are immediate. Otherwise m=|D| is an even positive
integer, m>=2, and both endpoint coefficients are strictly positive.

2. TWIST / COMMON-CORE / ZERO-COEFFICIENT AUDIT
Define the positive reciprocal twist by the FULL set T:

 h_T(x)=x^T h(y), y_i=1/x_i for i in T, y_i=x_i otherwise.

Multiaffinity cancels denominators, and the new coefficient of x^U is
c_U=f(T symmetric-difference U). Since Re(1/x)>0 iff Re(x)>0, and x^T does
not vanish in the right-half-plane domain, h_T is stable there. Its coefficients
remain nonnegative. Since |T| is even, its support remains even.

Now set all variables outside D to zero. Boundary specialization preserves
stability or gives the zero polynomial; the zero alternative is impossible
because its constant coefficient is c_empty=f(T)>0. For completeness, take
all those variables to a positive epsilon, obtaining stable polynomials, and
apply Hurwitz to their locally uniform limit. Denote the resulting polynomial
by

 g(x_D)=sum_{U subset D, |U| even} c_U x^U.

Its full coefficient is c_D=f(T symmetric-difference D)=f(S)>0.

The common occupied core causes no loss here. Original coefficients of g are
f(T symmetric-difference U) evaluated on the FULL ambient V; there is no
replacement by a smaller F, and no attempt to merge determinant orientations.
The core remains encoded in those coefficients. If S and T share hole indices,
twisting the full T BEFORE the outside-zero specialization handles them too;
twisting only T\D would generally acquire the wrong endpoint coefficients.

3. EXACT ODD-DEGREE REDUCTION
For arbitrary weights w_j>0, j in J=D\{a}, set x_a=1 and x_j=w_j z. Define

 p_w(z)=g(1,(w_j z)_{j in J})=sum_{k=0}^{m-1} a_k z^k.

For Re(z)>0 all free variables have positive real part and x_a=1 is interior,
so p_w is nonvanishing in the open right half-plane. It has real nonnegative
coefficients. Its degree is EXACTLY d=m-1, an odd integer: multiaffinity gives
the upper bound, and c_D>0 gives its nonzero leading coefficient. Put
W=product_{j in J}w_j. The four coefficients required are exactly

 a_0=c_empty=f(T),
 a_d=c_D W=f(S)W,
 a_1=sum_{j in J} c_{a,j} w_j,

Internally proved, with a self-contained elementary proof below. Every nonnegative

inequality. In particular, the proposed real-stable signed even-hole polynomials
satisfy the generalized six-hole inequality, and the theorem covers an arbitrary
shared occupied core. It is stronger than a theorem about a six-by-six Hermitian
matrix. The exchange constant one is optimal, including in the hard-BCS matrix
subclass.

This closes the specified coefficient-exchange gate. It does not prove the
determinant-state sampler's transition, microscopic two-replica energy, or
congestion bounds, and it does not establish an FPRAS by itself. Novelty of the
exchange inequality remains a separate literature question.

EXACT THEOREM / INTERFACE

Let E be a finite set. Let f:2^E -> [0,infinity) vanish on all sets of one parity,
and define the multiaffine polynomial h(x)=sum_U f(U) product_{i in U} x_i.
Assume h is nonzero and Hurwitz stable: h(z) != 0 whenever Re z_i > 0 for all i.
For all S,T in 2^E of the supported parity and every a in D=S symmetric-difference
T, the following inequality holds:

 sqrt(f(S) f(T)) <=
 sum_{j in D, j != a} sqrt(f(S symmetric-difference {a,j})
                          f(T symmetric-difference {a,j})).             (E)

If f(S)f(T)=0, (E) is immediate. If S=T, there is no a to quantify over. Otherwise
|D| is a positive even integer. No homogeneity, ordinary positive-coefficient
log-concavity, determinant representation, graph structure, or genericity is
assumed. The coefficients may be zero and the polynomial may have boundary
zeros on Re z_i=0.

For the exact form in the cycle-4 task, n=|E| is even and

 Q(x)=sum_{U even} (-1)^((n-|U|)/2) f(U) x^U

is real stable in the upper half-plane. Then
h(x)=(-1)^(n/2) Q(i x)=sum_{U even}f(U)x^U is Hurwitz stable, so (E) applies.
The rotation maps Re x_i>0 to Im(i x_i)>0. This is the place where the signed
stable polynomial enters; it is not a claim that its unsigned coefficient
polynomial is stable in the upper half-plane or log-concave.

Lemma. Let p(z)=a_0+a_1 z+...+a_d z^d be a real polynomial of odd degree d with

Proof. All its roots rho_i satisfy Re rho_i<=0; none is zero because a_0>0.
Put r_i=-1/rho_i. Then Re r_i>=0 and

perturbation assumption. For d=1 the assertion is equality.
